ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $AD \perp BC$, $AE$ bisects $\angle BAC$, $\angle B = 70^\circ$, $\angle C = 30^\circ$. What is the measure of $\angle DAE$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AD \perp BC$, \\
it follows that $\angle ADC=90^\circ$, \\
which implies $\angle DAC=90^\circ - \angle C=60^\circ$, \\
thus $\angle DAE=\angle DAC - \angle EAC=\boxed{20^\circ}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, BC is the base, and A is above; D and E are both on BC, and from left to right they are B, D, E, C in order. Segment AD is perpendicular from A to the base BC, and segment AE connects from A to E, located between AD and AC. The problem statement gives AD ⟂ BC, AE bisects ∠BAC, ∠B=70°, ∠C=30°. Reasoning: The sum of the interior angles of a triangle is 180°, so ∠BAC=180°−70°−30°=80°. Because AE bisects ∠BAC, ∠EAC=80°/2=40°. Also because AD ⟂ BC, in right triangle ADC, ∠ADC=90°, and ∠ACD=∠C=30°, therefore ∠DAC=180°−90°−30°=60°. It can be seen from the figure that AE is located between AD and AC, so ∠DAE=∠DAC−∠EAC=60°−40°=20°.
